title: Cardinal Ops partnership scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick internal scratch for Cardinal Ops (logistics SaaS) outbound / discovery. Keep messy.

Summary takeaways (first pass):
- Vertical: logistics / last-mile / carrier network management.
- Use case signals: automated status summaries for shippers, SLA-aware rerouting, customer chat triage (refunds/damage claims).
- Data sensitivity: PII (addresses), contract rates, contract SLAs => they will push for Private or Dedicated.
- Size: ~480 employees (Glassdoor + LinkedIn), series B (2023), estimated 200–500k shipments/month (claim figure from investor deck).
- Tech hints: Postgres, Kafka, k8s on AWS, internal microservices. CTO = Lena Ortiz, Head of Data = Marcus Ye, Product = Jonah Ruiz (mobile + ops).

Why Redwood fits (angles to lean on):
- Predictable latency for chat/real-time routing decisions (Dedicated pools, autoscale burst).
- Data residency + auditability for contracts -> Private (VPC) option + KMS/HSM integration.
- Cost controls: Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + KV caching) minimize per-token cost for high-volume telemetry->summary flows.
- Rollouts + safety: canary/AB routes + fallback to smaller model variants if latency spikes.

Key unknowns / research to validate next:
- Who owns ML/infra? (is it Head of Data or Platform Eng?) -> need org map.
- Are they using any hosted model providers currently (OpenAI, Anthropic) for chat? check code hints on GitHub or job posts.
- Typical request sizes: how long are their customer summaries? (avg token length)

Outbound sequence (short):
1) Cold email -> brief signal + ask for 20m to show predictable latency + demo of reductions in token cost on similar workloads.
2) Follow-up -> one-pager: "LLM for operations at scale" (attach lightweight PDF) + invite to 1:1 pilot sync.
3) If no reply -> LinkedIn note to CTO + short technical note to Head of Data referencing model latency benchmarks.

Cold email draft (short, keep for A/B):
Subject: Cardinal Ops + predictable LLM inference for ops & routing
Hi Lena — saw Cardinal Ops’ talk at FreightTech (great threading on SLA guarantees). Quick question: are you evaluating model providers for operational summaries / routing assistance? We’ve helped companies reduce per-transaction inference cost by ~35% while keeping 99th-pct latency stable with a dedicated GPU pool + prefix caching.
If helpful I can share a 15–20m demo + quick cost projection for 100k monthly summaries.
— Asha (Redwood)

Alternative A/B subject: "Cut LLM inference latency for routing decisions (pilot)"

Discovery agenda (if meeting booked):
- 5m intros/what they measure for SLA/latency today
- 10m walk-through of potential flows (summary generation, triage chat, reroute decisioning) with baseline metrics
- 10m pilot design: data paths, privacy constraints, success metrics (latency at p99, cost per summary, false-action rate)
- Next steps: sample data exchange, infra assessment, timeline + pilot SOW

Objections: expected + quick rebuttals (working notes)
- "Cost too high" -> Anchor: we can start with hosted API for discovery (no infra lift), show cost numbers, then move to Dedicated or Private for predictability. Offer a small pilot credit to run 1 week of real traffic. Emphasize Optimize-led config reduces unit cost vs naive endpoints.
- "Data residency/compliance concerns" -> Private deployment with customer-controlled VPC + KMS. Show compliance pack and audit logs sample.
- "Integration complexity / engineering lift" -> Provide SDKs (node/python) + example repo for Kafka consumer -> Redwood request router. Offer Solutions Eng pairing during first sprint.
- "Model hallucinations / safety" -> talk about evaluation harness, prompt sets, regression alerts tied to evals in Redwood Console. Default to smaller, more calibrated model variants for routing decisions (few-shot templates + reranking).
- "Latency spikes during peak batch" -> route policy + fallback to cheaper model variants or region. Show autoscale + burst options.

Pilot hypothesis (one-liner):
If we serve routing summaries and triage chat through a Dedicated Redwood pool with prefix/KV caching, we can meet p99 latency target of <= 300ms for short summaries and reduce per-summary token cost by 25–40% vs current hosted endpoints.

Pilot scope (minimal):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2w integration, 2w baseline run, 2w optimizations)
- Data: sanitized subset of events (anonymized addresses) OR via Private VPC connector (their preference)
- Success metrics: p99 latency, per-summary cost, error rate (hallucination/failure)
- Roles: Redwood SE (Rafael), Cardinal Eng lead (TBD), Security review (Priya)

Internal TODOs & tickets:
- Draft small one-pager for pricing (anchor numbers): dev/POC tier = $6k/month for dedicated baseline (estimate) + usage. Need finance sign-off. (create ticket GROW-214 on Jira) -> linked.
- Build sample Kafka -> Redwood connector example (reuse code from partner-sdks PR#78). Assign to dev: Rafael.
- Prep privacy packet + de-id checklist for Private deployment. Priya to own.
- Ask Marcus Ye (Head of Data) if they have any internal latency SLOs for decision systems (email / LinkedIn).

Notes to self (messy):
- Could also propose a hybrid: start hosted for feature discovery -> move to Dedicated with VPC once we prove quality. That reduces initial procurement friction.
- If Legal/Procurement asks for SLA language, have NDA + pilot statement ready (template exists in sales folder).
- Pricing thought: anchor POC at $6k–12k/mo depending on qPS + model choice. Include 2-week pilot credit.

Call prep checklist (if intro booked):
- Deck: 6 slides (problem, how Redwood solves, short demo, pilot ask, pricing, next steps) -> use partner-deck template
- Live demo: run a short summary generation (sanitize examples) -> ensure we show p99 latency trace in Console
- Bring SE (Rafael) + Solutions Eng notes on integration path (kafka->http gateway)

Potential escalation signals:
- If they mention procurement requiring annual contract -> highlight Dedicated reserved capacity options + support tiers.
- If they ask for on-prem -> note Redwood Private on-prem package (needs SE + 4–6 week lead time).

Questions I still have:
- What are their monthly token volumes for chat vs summaries? (estimate from shipments/month?)
- Does their security team prefer tenant-isolated infra or fully customer managed?
- Are there any performance benchmarks publicly cited? (search investor deck again)

Next steps (this week):
- Send cold email (A/B) and LinkedIn note to Lena -> target Mon 2026-03-16
- Rafael to spin up Kafka->Redwood sample branch from PR#78 this week (assign)
- Priya to assemble privacy checklist and one-pager by Tue
- Create pilot pricing stub in GROW-214 and route to Finance for quick take

End of scratchpad. Keep updates here as replies/notes from prospect arrive.
